datasets.name: ds_daily
queryLines:
SELECT date_trunc('DAY', event_hour) AS day,
       sum(views) AS views, sum(carts) AS carts, sum(purchases) AS purchases, sum(revenue) AS revenue
FROM product_conversion_hourly
GROUP BY date_trunc('DAY', event_hour)
ORDER BY day

datasets.name: ds_acceptance
queryLines:
WITH titles AS (SELECT * FROM VALUES ('A1', 1, 'Two independent feeds'), ('A2', 2, '>= 200 products change > 15%'), ('A3', 3, 'Own 30-minute sessions'), ('A4', 4, 'Temporal join: 3 strategies compared'), ('A5', 5, 'Price binding accuracy'), ('A6', 6, 'Schema evolution, no files rewritten'), ('A7', 7, 'Clustering evolution, no files rewritten'), ('A8', 8, 'Compaction measured'), ('A9', 9, 'Q1 elasticity'), ('A10', 10, 'Q2 lost revenue, two definitions'), ('A11', 11, 'Q3 frozen copy + retention'), ('A12', 12, 'Serving: stats, MV, three-way') AS t(id, ord, criterion)),
latest AS (
  SELECT substr(metric, 12) AS id, value AS status, step AS proved_by, recorded_at,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY metric ORDER BY recorded_at DESC) AS r
  FROM ops.measurements
  WHERE metric LIKE 'acceptance\\_A%'
)
SELECT t.ord, t.id, t.criterion, coalesce(l.status, 'NOT RUN') AS status, l.proved_by, l.recorded_at
FROM titles t LEFT JOIN latest l ON l.id = t.id AND l.r = 1
ORDER BY t.ord

datasets.name: ds_q1_floors
queryLines:
WITH floors AS (SELECT explode(array(1, 5, 10, 30)) AS floor)
SELECT f.floor,
       concat('>= ', f.floor, ' purchases') AS floor_label,
       count(e.product_id) AS drops_qualifying,
       percentile_approx(e.elasticity, 0.5) AS median_elasticity,
       avg(CASE WHEN e.product_id IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN e.post_purchases = 0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END)
         AS share_no_post_purchase
FROM floors f
LEFT JOIN price_elasticity e
  ON e.base_purchases >= f.floor AND e.pct_price_change < 0 AND e.elasticity IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY f.floor
ORDER BY f.floor

datasets.name: ds_q1_drops
datasets.displayName: Q1 price drops at the headline floor
queryLines:
SELECT product_id, category_id, changed_at, original_price, new_price, pct_price_change,
       base_purchases, base_purchases_per_2h, post_purchases, post_purchases_per_2h, elasticity
FROM price_elasticity
WHERE pct_price_change < 0 AND base_purchases >= 5 AND elasticity IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY elasticity

datasets.name: ds_q2_carts
queryLines:
SELECT product_id, category_id, session_key, carted_at, changed_at, price_at_cart,
       price_before_increase, pct_price_change, lost_revenue_at_cart, lost_revenue_at_old
FROM cart_abandonment

datasets.name: ds_q2_top
queryLines:
SELECT category_id,
       count(DISTINCT session_key) AS sessions,
       count(*) AS carts,
       sum(lost_revenue_at_cart) AS lost_at_cart_price,
       sum(lost_revenue_at_old) AS lost_at_old_price
FROM cart_abandonment
GROUP BY category_id
ORDER BY lost_at_cart_price DESC, category_id
LIMIT 10

datasets.name: ds_q3
queryLines:
WITH frozen AS (
  SELECT category_id, sum(purchases) AS purchases, sum(revenue) AS revenue
  FROM audit.product_conversion_hourly_black_friday_2026_final GROUP BY category_id),
live AS (
  SELECT category_id, sum(purchases) AS purchases, sum(revenue) AS revenue
  FROM product_conversion_hourly GROUP BY category_id)
SELECT coalesce(f.category_id, l.category_id) AS category_id,
       f.purchases AS frozen_purchases, l.purchases AS live_purchases,
       f.revenue AS frozen_revenue, l.revenue AS live_revenue,
       coalesce(l.purchases, 0) - coalesce(f.purchases, 0) AS purchases_drift,
       CASE WHEN coalesce(l.purchases, 0) = coalesce(f.purchases, 0)
             AND coalesce(l.revenue, 0) = coalesce(f.revenue, 0)
            THEN 'unchanged' ELSE 'moved' END AS live_vs_frozen
FROM frozen f FULL OUTER JOIN live l ON f.category_id = l.category_id
ORDER BY frozen_revenue DESC NULLS LAST

lines: Fourteen days of a cosmetics shop's clickstream, rebuilt as a medallion lakehouse on Databricks Free Edition. The pages answer the exam's three questions: **Q1** price elasticity, **Q2** carts abandoned after a price increase, **Q3** a frozen Black Friday audit.

frame.title: Acceptance criteria, latest result of each

lines: ## Q1 · What happens to purchases after a price drop of more than 15%?

Baseline: the original price's own interval, up to 7 days before the change. Post: the 2 hours after, while the new price holds. Both normalised to 2-hour blocks. A drop counts only if its baseline has at least the floor's number of purchases.

frame.title: Price drops that clear each volume floor

y.displayName: No purchase in the 2 h after

frame.title: …of which had no purchase at all in the 2 hours after

lines: **How to read this.** When the 2 hours after a drop hold no purchase, the purchase change is −100% and elasticity is exactly −1 ÷ price change: a *positive* number for a drop. That comes from the window's length, not from demand. Confounders this data cannot rule out: time of day, promotions, stock-outs, competitor prices, when the change was observed, and small counts.

frame.title: Price drops at the headline floor (≥ 5 baseline purchases)

lines: ## Q2 · Carts abandoned within 30 minutes of a price increase

Lost revenue two ways: at the price shown when the item was carted (headline) and at the price before the increase (sensitivity). The gap is what the increase was meant to earn. Grouped by category_id, because category_code is missing for 98% of events.
